title: An affine coherent algebra realization with proper support is finite and proper
statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], f : X -> S locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and g : Y -> X affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let B be a commutative O_X-algebra sheaf [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf] with an O_X-algebra isomorphism B -> g_*O_Y. If the underlying module of B is coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and has support proper over S [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base], then g is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and g followed by f is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 09ZT, last sentence, finite and properness clauses; Lemma 0CYS (3)

proof.text: Coherence on the locally Noetherian scheme gives quasi-coherence and finite type. Restrict finite local generators to the slice over an open U: the restricted cover still covers, and its pushforward functors preserve colimits and the unit, so their images are finite generating families. On affine U the finite-type affine criterion makes the sections finite. The component of the algebra isomorphism is a surjective linear map from these sections to Γ(Y, g inverse U), with scalars restricted along g.app U; linearity follows from the Under morphism equation and multiplicativity. Transport finite generation along this map. Apply Mathlib isFinite_iff to conclude that g is finite; the assumed IsAffineHom supplies affineness directly, with no relative-spectrum equivalence.

Apply module_support_proper_over_base to obtain a closed immersion i : Z → X such that i followed by f is proper and i.ker kills B. For a section a of i.ker on an affine open, apply annihilation to 1 in B: the structure map sends a to zero. The Under morphism equation for the algebra isomorphism then implies g.app sends a to zero. Thus i.ker ≤ g.ker. Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.lift constructs l : Y → Z with l followed by i = g. Since g is finite and i is separated, IsFinite.of_comp makes l finite. Finite morphisms are proper and proper morphisms compose, so l followed by i followed by f is proper, hence g followed by f is proper. These arguments use no nonemptiness or nonzero-ring hypotheses.
